correctness.rationale: The squared-axis gap is exactly the discriminant of the compression of diag(eta,0,-Delta) to the viewing plane, yielding (eta-(eta+Delta)x^2-Delta y^2)^2+4 eta Delta y^2. Near-roundness localizes to x^2+y^2=O(eta); scaling x,y by sqrt(Delta/eta) yields the Cassini inequality |1-z^2|<t. The exact spherical area Jacobian gives probability eta/(2pi Delta) times Cassini area and normalized conditional area. The square-map Jacobian gives area as one half the integral of 1/|w| over |w-1|<t, evaluated in complete elliptic integrals with the correct factor 4. Differentiating shows the logarithmic singularity at t=1. Algebraic boundaries have area zero, legitimating dominated convergence. A runnable checker compared direct compression eigengaps, independent quadratures and the analytic scaling at t below, at, and above 1. No finite test was promoted to an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Existing general triaxial projection formulas and the prior fixed-shape central-section near-circular coefficient are explicitly credited and excluded from the new claim. Orthogonal shadows are planar polars of central sections of the polar ellipsoid, so the earlier fixed-anisotropy coefficient transfers exactly; it cannot be substituted into a simultaneous eta-and-threshold limit because it is not uniform in the spectral gap. The new mathematical object is the uniform Cassini-oval double scaling with a logarithmic merger at t=1, not a re-expression of the fixed-shape coefficient. No prior statement of this joint limit was identified in the inspected primary sources or semantic/source queries. Specialized optics literature remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: Random orientation inference for triaxial bodies makes almost-circular shadows a natural statistic. Fixed-triaxial quadratic probability scaling and axisymmetric linear scaling are incompatible under naive extrapolation. The joint limit interpolates them through an explicit universal nonconstant function and identifies a previously hidden topology and logarithmic regularity transition of conditional viewing directions. This is a structural, geometrically motivated asymptotic law rather than a numerical table entry or an arbitrary special parameter slice.
